fig1_architecture.png: Model arms. (a) Feature-token models: each feature is one token; the mixer is multi-head attention or a token-wise affine control. (b) Single-token models from the original design (T = 1), with attention or an affine control.
fig2_cv_auc_onehot.png: ROC-AUC across the 50 held-out folds. Dots: folds; marker: mean; bar: corrected 95% CI; right: mean ± SD.
fig3_pairwise_onehot.png: Paired ROC-AUC differences over the same 50 folds, with the Nadeau-Bengio corrected 95% CI and Holm-adjusted p-values.
fig4_roc_onehot.png: Fold-averaged ROC curves for six models.
fig5_learning_onehot.png: Training histories for the five folds of repeat 1. Solid: fitting subset; dashed: inner validation subset; dot: epoch whose weights were restored.
fig6_shap_importance.png: Kernel SHAP importance per model, same explainer, background and patients (every patient explained out of fold, 3 repeats). Shade: share of the model's total mean |SHAP|; number: rank.
fig7_rank_agreement.png: Agreement of SHAP importance rankings between models (Spearman ρ; bracket: lower bound of the patient-bootstrap 95% CI).
fig8_attention.png: Feature-token attention. (a) Attention received vs mean |SHAP| per feature; dotted: uniform attention (1/13). (b) Mean attention map over 50 folds, shown as the deviation from uniform attention.
fig9_external.png: Trained on Cleveland, tested on three other UCI sites, on the 8 features recorded at every site. External: mean over 10 seeds, patient-bootstrap 95% CI; Cleveland: 10 x 5 CV on the same 8 features.
fig10_encoding_sensitivity.png: Encoding sensitivity: one-hot nominal variables (main) vs the original z-scored integer codes, same 50 folds.
fig11_ablation.png: Head count x attention dropout for the feature-token attention model, same 50 folds (mean ± SD ROC-AUC; colour scale fixed at 0.85-0.95).
